The unprecedented participation has already set new capital market records, breaking the Nigerian market record on its opening day and surpassing the previous African record within its first ten days, driven by strong demand from retail investors, pension funds and institutional investors.
Continental confidence has been reinforced by the refinery’s strong financial turnaround and a fresh valuation upgrade.
Renaissance Capital Africa (RCA) has lifted its valuation of the refinery to N700.41 per share, implying a 33.4 per cent upside from the IPO offer price of N525 per share.
In its October 16, 2026 update titled ‘Stronger Refining Margins Drive Earnings Outperformance’, RCA said the upgrade reflects exceptional earnings performance in the first nine months of 2026, driven by stronger refining margins and better-than-anticipated operational results.
For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, Dangote Refinery reported revenue of $22.5 billion and net profit of $4.7 billion, one of the strongest performances by an African industrial enterprise. This marks a sharp turnaround from a loss of $117.2 million in the same period of 2025.
Revenue grew 144 per cent from $9.2 billion, EBITDA increased nearly nine-fold to $5.5 billion from $627.6 million, while operating cash flow rose more than ten-fold to $3.68 billion. The company also moved from a net debt position of $1.73 billion in September 2025 to a net cash position of $651 million by September 2026.
The chief financial officer of Dangote Group, Murat Erden, said the performance has already exceeded the assumptions underpinning the IPO valuation.
“This offering represents far more than a capital-raising exercise. It is a landmark opportunity for Africans to participate in the ownership of one of the continent’s most transformative industrial assets,” Erden said.
“Our financial performance has already advanced well beyond the baseline assumptions used in determining the IPO valuation. The extraordinary participation from 51 African countries is a shared conviction that Africans should not only benefit from industrial development but also own and create wealth from it,” he added.
The transaction has also benefited from pioneering cross-border collaborations involving Botswana, Egypt, Ethiopia and Kenya, which the company described as a blueprint for future continent-wide offerings.
The offer, which provides potential for USD-linked dividends, will close on October 27, 2026.
